§12.1.1 Images

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

images-images · rule images

✅ Normative

The content of an image MUST be put into the text stream as whatever the image actually is — transcribed text, a table or a diagram. The output MUST NOT contain a file reference or a bracketed placeholder in place of an image.

An image is not a thing to point at; it is content that happens to have been rasterised. Whatever a reader would take away from looking at it MUST end up in the output as text, or it is lost — the never drop failure.

Decide what the image is, then encode that

The image is really… The output MUST contain
Text rendered as a picture The text, transcribed verbatim
A data display (chart, plot) A chart table — Cover Every Data Point§11.1.1
A labelled schematic or conceptual figure A suitable diagram/<language> block; description only if none can preserve it — Slide Diagrams§12.2.5
A graph of relationships or a flow A diagram/<language> fenced block (for example diagram/mermaid or diagram/plantUml) — Diagrams and Flowcharts§12.2.2
A photo or decorative art A prose description of what it shows

The rows are tried in order. Where any text at all is legible inside the image, that text MUST be transcribed: it is content, and describing it instead ("a chart showing quarterly revenue") drops every number on the page.

When the type is not obvious

Some figures resist the table above: maps, chemical structures, electrical schematics, blueprints, printed staves. Each has its own rule — Geographic Maps§12.2.4, Chemical Molecules§13.1, Electrical Schematics§12.2.3, Blueprints§12.2.1, Music Notation§13.2, Slide Diagrams§12.2.5. Where that rule has no settled encoding yet, the fallback is the same: every label and every legible string MUST be preserved, and the output MUST use the encoding that loses no content.
